text:
ashwin: Quick spike summary — thinking about per-customer precision SLAs + routing. We can expose a 'precision policy' on the serving side that maps customer_id -> {max_latency_ms, min_quality_score, cost_tolerance} and have smart router pick FP8/INT8/4bit/FP16 variants. Thoughts?
kevin: Love the idea. Main concern: how do we quantify min_quality_score? e.g., use eval-suite BLEU/ROUGE? customer-facing metrics need to be conservative.
maria: We should use CustomerQA and a set of golden prompts per customer slice. not global BLEU. also add per-domain thresholds (summaries vs code gen).
taylor: Ops question: how expensive is routing decision? do we want per-request model quality prediction or sample-based enforcement? runtime needs to be O(1).
luis: Proposal: two-stage enforcement
luis: 1) compile-time precision policy -> choose allowed model variants per route
luis: 2) runtime quick-check using lightweight quality estimator (tiny classifier on prompt+meta) that outputs pass/fail
ashwin: Example of serving config sketch:

``
precision_policy:
  name: "enterprise-tier"
  allowed_variants: ["fp8-fast", "int8-balanced"]
  min_quality: 0.92
  latency_slo_ms: 120
  rollout: {canary: 0.05, region_fallback: true}
```

maria: That min_quality 0.92 — what metric? Recommend using 'degradation_score' (0-1) computed from prompt-level evals + calibration offsets per model.
kevin: Need to avoid heavy per-request evals. lightweight estimator idea is good; we can train on cached KV-prefixes and prompt embeddings. cheap inference on CPU.
taylor: Fallback policy: if estimator says fail -> route to a slower but higher-precision variant or queue for retry. Do we want immediate fallback or async re-run? For low-latency product maybe immediate fallback preferred.
ashwin: Rollout plan idea: canary by customer for 2 weeks with metric hooks: per-request degradation_score, tokens/cost, 95p latency, and ERR (error rate). perf-bot will ping on regressions > 2%.
perf-bot: Automated alert rule: when per-customer avg degradation_score drops > 0.03 vs baseline and 95p latency > configured SLO -> alert #eng-oncall
luis: Edge case: mixed-content sessions (chat + code). Policy should be route-by-turn not just by-session. also add hysteresis so we don't flip per message.
maria: For long-term architecture we should build a 'precision policy compiler' — high-level DSL -> validated routing graph + runtime checks + certs for SLA. This will make audits easier for Private deployments.
kevin: Implementation constraints: runtime must keep decision table in RAM with O(1) lookup; integrate with existing smart router (region/cost). Also ensure tracing has precision_variant choice.
taylor: Telemetry additions: sample 1% of decisions for ground-truth eval (full eval suite) to continuously update model-specific calibration offsets.
ashwin: Action items:
 - ashwin: prototype lightweight estimator (deadline: 2w)
 - maria: sketch policy DSL with degradation_score semantics (1w)
 - luis: design fallback hysteresis and per-turn routing rules (1w)
 - kevin: add tracing hooks + telemetry spec (3d)
 - taylor: add canary playbook entries for per-customer precision routing (3d)

ashwin: any other blockers? :thinking:
kevin: One more: legal/compliance — customers need opt-out for cross-variant fallback if they require fixed-precision for audits.
maria: Noted. add 'enforce_fixed_precision: true/false' to the policy schema.
ashwin: Cool. I'll spin up a repo with a toy router and share results in a follow-up thread. Thanks all :rocket:
